limitations: Electricity values are national or territorial estimates, not local household observations.
Life expectancy is a national or territorial period mean; the population distribution groups people by territorial context and is not a person-level lifespan distribution.
GDP per capita is a territorial national-accounts context value in constant 2015 US dollars; it is not individual income, household wealth, or a purchasing-power-parity welfare ranking.
The covered universe is reconciled to WLD with an explicit residual but lacks source-coded parent/dependency relations.
The 1:110m display geometry omits some small territories; their population remains in summaries.
Pre-1960 historical population is a global estimate or source-disagreement range and is not spatially allocated.
Cliopatria polygons and labels are contestable historical context, simplified for display, and never used as population supports.
Only selected Cliopatria snapshot years are published; the effective boundary date is shown separately from the requested date.

Ancient-city points appear only at exact published dates; coordinates are source geocodes, modern-country labels are descriptive metadata, and city estimates are not summed as total urban or world population.
UN WPP values are modeled population estimates through 2023 and Medium projections from 2024; projection scenarios are not confidence intervals.
WPP Country/Area supports are shown on available modern Natural Earth display geometry and are not claims about historical political borders.
The reconciliation decision set links source records and annotates source-declared hierarchy but never merges observations, edits source geometry, or assigns population to political features.
Twenty bounded 1500 CE border overlaps and two coordinate-only city identities remain explicitly unresolved because current source evidence does not adjudicate them.
Country color still represents a territorial total; when selected, grid columns separately show source-native modeled population per one-degree bin.
Grid bins are aggregated by source-pixel centre and are not exact one-degree footprints or borders. No grid population is allocated to political entities.
GHSL starts in 1975; this release does not spatialize earlier global population estimates. WorldPop is a separate source, not a replacement or splice.
Economic evidence is a set of source-native country/economy tables, not a reconstruction of economic activity within historical borders or every human population.

Maddison 2023 starts at 1 CE for a small set of supports; no economic observation is asserted for 10000 BCE–1 BCE. Its original-source sheet references are country-level candidates, not verified per-observation provenance.
Economic indicators have distinct units, supports, methods, releases, and year coverage; this release does not merge them into a score or interpolate missing dates.

PIP survey Gini and decile shares use country-specific income or consumption welfare; they are not WDI Gini, wealth inequality, or one uniform global welfare concept. Multiple surveys in one country-year remain separate.

PWT TFP is a model-based productivity level (USA=1), not output per labor-hour; employment and hours are separate inputs, not an Atlas-derived labor-productivity series. Country supports are not historical polities.
V-Dem country-year coding units are not joined to Cliopatria historical borders, modern population weights, or a global institutional score.
V-Dem ordinal religion-policy categories are source-authored expert-model outputs, not direct measures of each person's rights or religious identity.
Religious composition is not yet published: Pew needs account/terms review, Seshat Equinox contains conflicting license notices, and WRP/ARDA require reuse review.

Chandler and Modelski companion estimates are separate source series. A shared place link never averages or replaces values, and the two Chandler zero cells remain quarantined as unresolved source codes.
UCDP/PRIO ACD rows are source conflict-years, not a complete absence-of-violence panel or a political-border overlay.
UCDP OrganizedViolenceCY country-years use Gleditsch-Ward supports and GED-derived within-border estimates; zeros have UCDP's inclusion-threshold meaning, not proof of peace.
Four OrganizedViolenceCY rows have low/best/high fatality estimates out of numerical order; the three fields are retained independently, never rendered as a confidence interval.
The UCDP GED event archive remains acquired but unpublished pending event-location semantics and the separate 5,075 nonmonotonic event-bound review.
